examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Default dropdown with a single unlabeled group of six options and no left/right affordances. Click the trigger to open; controls drive side, align, sideOffset, and disabled.

examples.name: Groups
examples.summary: Two labeled groups (`Account`, `Workspace`) separated by an automatic top divider on the second group. One option carries a `command` hint, another is `selected` — the central anatomy of this component.

examples.name: States
examples.summary: Click the trigger to open the panel and see each spec-declared option state side-by-side: `default`, `selected`, and `disabled`. The `hover` and `focus-visible` states are interactive — focus an option with the keyboard (`Down` / `Up`) or hover with the pointer to see them.

examples.name: Placements
examples.summary: The four corners (`side` `bottom` / `top` × `align` `start` / `end`) side-by-side. Click each trigger to see how the panel anchors against it. Panels are teleported to `body` and positioned with `position: fixed` against the trigger's bounding rect — no external positioning runtime.

examples.name: AutoPlacement
examples.summary: `side="auto"` lets the dropdown choose the side with the most room at open time. The four triggers below all use the same prop value — each resolves to a different side based on the available space around them. The resolved value is reflected in `data-side` on the open panel.

examples.name: OptionAffordances
examples.summary: Click the trigger to see every option affordance: plain label, `command` keyboard hint, `leading` icon slot, `trailing` content slot (with a `Tag`), `selected` state (a checked radio item with a check mark), and `disabled` state. The `command` prop and the `trailing` slot are mutually exclusive — pick one per option.

examples.name: WithHeaderAndFooter
examples.summary: Click the trigger to open the panel with the root `header` and `footer` named slots in use — typically a search input at the top and a footer action at the bottom. Both regions stick to their edges and stay outside the scrollable group list.

examples.name: GroupsWithHeaderAndFooter
examples.summary: Click the trigger to open two groups each using the `header` and `footer` slots — a per-section caption above the options and a footer action below. Different from the root `header`/`footer` (which are sticky outside the scroll area), group-level slots render inline within the section.

examples.name: SubMenus
examples.summary: `DropdownMenu.Sub` nests a menu: `SubTrigger` is the row with the chevron and `SubContent` the panel beside it. It opens on hover, click, `Enter`, `Space` or `ArrowRight`; `ArrowLeft` or `Esc` closes it. Click the trigger to open the menu: `Move to` opens with it (`default-open`) and holds a second level; `Share` is disabled.

examples.name: CheckableOptions
examples.summary: `type="checkbox"` and `type="radio"` turn options into `menuitemcheckbox` / `menuitemradio` items with a check or dot and `aria-checked`. They keep the panel open on activation, so several columns can be toggled in a row; `selected` comes from your own state in the `select` handler.

examples.name: CustomTriggers
examples.summary: `DropdownMenu.Trigger` is abstract — it wires `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` and the open/close click onto whatever element you put inside its default slot. Here it wraps an `IconButton` (row actions) and an `Avatar` (account menu).
